original_context: Logic and notation: Iverson bracket [P] returns numeric 1 when proposition P is true and 0 otherwise. In the Kronecker delta definition P is the equality predicate a=b on Γ; the general Iverson notation applies to arbitrary propositions, not merely to equality.
definition: For a mathematical proposition P, the Iverson bracket [P] is the numerical value 1 when P is true and 0 when P is false. This is a general indicator notation for the truth value of P.
reasoning: The independent population has the numeric Kronecker delta δ(a,b)=[a=b], but its equality-specific two-argument meaning does not define Iverson brackets for arbitrary propositions. Iverson brackets are a general named notation/construction, so retain this independent meaning rather than merging it into the Kronecker delta.

sources.relevance: Directly verified general statement-truth-value notation and its numeric 0/1 values.

related_screened_meanings.relation: Equality-specific numerical Kronecker delta is a specialization [a=b] and cannot replace arbitrary P

comparison.rationale: Reviewed the indexed formulations of all 595 independently screened and 16 provisional meanings. Only the equality-specific numeric Kronecker delta refers to Iverson indicators; the general bracket is not already a meaning and is a standard named mathematical notation. Also compared with the already staged first-generation candidate identities: missing.8e10ca4c4067ac5928f8, missing.8e7388ef8958ac46b761; none has this same mathematical object or proposition.

mathematical_assumptions: Values are ordinary integers 0 and 1, not an identification inside a zero ring.
The proposition has a determinate truth value in the ambient logic.
Floor-function brackets use a distinct convention and should be disambiguated by context.
